title: Short Second Proof of the Odd-Modulus Directed Torus Hamilton Decomposition Theorem
summary: Let $D_d(m)=\operatorname{Cay}((\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^d,\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\})$, with all generators oriented positively. We give a second proof that $D_d(m)$ decomposes into $d$ directed Hamilton cycles for every $d\ge 2$ and every odd $m\ge 3$. The combinatorial core is a fixed-row-sum selection theorem for replicated supports: when each indexed support $A$ is repeated in $m$ identical rows, one can select $\lfloor |A|/2\rfloor$ entries from each row so that every column total is a unit modulo $m$.
